title: Working Together 2026: safeguarding partners, referral, s47 timescales, LADO and named professionals
blurb: Follow a referral through Working Together 2026, know every key timescale, and route allegations against staff to the LADO.
question: A mother tells a children's nurse that she saw a healthcare assistant grab her son roughly and swear at him overnight. The assistant is still on shift. What should the nurse do, and who must be told within one working day?

teach.body: Working Together to Safeguard Children 2026 (DfE, March 2026) is the statutory guidance for multi-agency safeguarding in England. It replaced the 2023 edition. It sets out who leads local arrangements, how referrals, assessments and child protection enquiries run, and the timescales. In plain English: it is the rulebook every agency follows when a child may need help or protection. Its new emphasis includes Family Help, child sexual abuse, group-based exploitation and online harm.

teach.caption: A joint and equal duty to make local arrangements (Children Act 2004 ss16E-16K). Each lead appoints a delegated safeguarding partner.

items.label: Social care decides next steps on a referral
Strategy discussion if significant harm suspected
Initial child protection conference after the strategy discussion
Core group meets after the conference
First review conference; then every 6 months at most

teach.caption: Any assessment (s17 or s47) is completed within 45 working days of the referral.

head: Step
Timescale
rows: Decision on next steps after referral
Within 15 working days of the strategy discussion
Within 10 working days of the ICPC
Rapid review after serious incident notification

teach.body: Where there is reasonable cause to suspect a child is suffering, or likely to suffer, significant harm, a strategy discussion decides on the child's welfare and plans rapid action. A local authority social worker, health practitioners and a police representative should, as a minimum, be involved. It can be held at referral or at any later point, and may start s47 enquiries.

rows.label: Role
values: Advice, training, good practice in the trust

teach.caption: Ambulance trusts and independent providers have a 'named professional'. ICBs also employ named GPs.

teach.body: Any allegation that someone who works with children has harmed a child should be reported immediately to a senior manager. The Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO) must be informed within one working day of all allegations. The LADO advises on the process and on referral to a regulator. Employers must also refer to the Disclosure and Barring Service when they remove someone from regulated activity because of risk of harm. The child's safety comes first throughout.

The nurse ensures the boy is safe, checks him for injury and asks the nurse in charge to ensure the assistant has no further contact with him. She reports immediately to the nurse in charge and senior manager, records the mother's account in her words, and informs the trust's named nurse. The trust informs the LADO within one working day. The nurse does not investigate or confront the assistant herself.

teach.text: Allegations against staff go to the LADO (within one working day), not through a standard s47 referral alone. And do not mix the clocks: 15 working days runs from strategy discussion to initial conference; 45 working days is the maximum for an assessment; 10 working days is the core group.

items: Safeguarding partners: local authority, ICB, chief officer of police.
Referral decision 1 working day; assessment 45 working days; ICPC 15 working days from strategy discussion; core group 10 working days; review 3 months then 6-monthly.
Strategy discussion: social care, health and police as a minimum.
Allegations against staff: senior manager now; LADO within 1 working day.
Named doctor and nurse in every NHS provider; designated doctor and nurse at the ICB.

summary: You can now follow a child from referral through strategy discussion, s47 enquiries and child protection conference, quoting each Working Together 2026 timescale. You can also route an allegation against a colleague to the LADO and name the health safeguarding roles.

A.q: On Monday morning a children's nurse makes a referral to children's social care about Leah, 4, who has unexplained bruising. By when should social care decide on next steps?
options: Within 1 working day
Within 3 working days
Within 10 working days
Within 45 working days
A.why: Working Together 2026 para 167: within one working day of a referral, social care acknowledges it and a manager decides next steps.

whyNot.1: Three working days is not a Working Together timescale for this step.
whyNot.2: 10 working days is the core group timescale.
whyNot.3: 45 working days is the maximum for completing an assessment.

A.q: Which three agencies are the statutory safeguarding partners in a local authority area in England?
options: Local authority, NHS trust and police
Local authority, ICB and police
Local authority, ICB and schools
ICB, police and probation service
A.why: The safeguarding partners are the local authority, the integrated care board and the chief officer of police.

whyNot.0: The health partner is the ICB, not individual NHS trusts.
whyNot.2: Schools are relevant agencies, not statutory safeguarding partners.
whyNot.3: The local authority is a partner; probation is not.

A.q: A nurse in an NHS trust's children's ED wants expert safeguarding advice about a toddler's injuries. Which role in the trust provides this?
options: The ICB's designated nurse
The Local Authority Designated Officer
The trust's named nurse for safeguarding
The Child Safeguarding Practice Review Panel
A.why: Each NHS provider has a named doctor and named nurse for safeguarding children, who advise staff and lead training.

whyNot.0: Designated professionals work at ICB level across the health economy.
whyNot.1: The LADO handles allegations against people working with children.
whyNot.3: The national panel commissions and oversees national child safeguarding practice reviews, not ward-level advice.

B.q: Section 47 enquiries are started at a strategy discussion about Mason, 2, who has an unexplained fracture. The health visitor asks when the initial child protection conference should be held. What is correct?
options: Within 1 working day of the strategy discussion ending
Within 10 working days of the referral
Within 45 working days of the referral
Within 15 working days of the strategy discussion
B.why: The initial child protection conference should take place within 15 working days of the strategy discussion at which s47 enquiries were initiated.

whyNot.0: One working day is the referral decision timescale.
whyNot.1: 10 working days is the core group timescale after the conference.
whyNot.2: 45 working days is the assessment maximum.

B.q: Ava, 7, became the subject of a child protection plan last week. Her school nurse is in the core group and asks when the first review conference should be held. What is correct?
options: Within 6 weeks of the initial conference
Within 3 months of the initial conference
Within 6 months of the initial conference
Within 12 months of the initial conference
B.why: The first review should be held within three months of the initial conference, then at intervals of no more than six months.

whyNot.0: Six weeks is not the review timescale.
whyNot.2: Six months is the maximum interval for later reviews, not the first.
whyNot.3: Twelve months is far too long.

B.q: Children's social care starts a Family Help assessment for Ollie, 6, after a referral about neglect. His father asks how long it can take. What is the maximum?
options: 15 working days from the referral
30 working days from the date of referral
45 working days from the referral
Within 3 months from the referral
B.why: Working Together 2026: the assessment should be no longer than 45 working days from the point of referral.

whyNot.0: 15 working days is the ICPC timescale.
whyNot.1: 30 working days is not the Working Together maximum.
whyNot.3: Three months is the first review conference timescale.

C.q: A healthcare assistant on a children's ward is seen slapping a 4-year-old. The child is safe and the nurse has told the nurse in charge. What must also happen within one working day?
options: The LADO is informed of the allegation
The NMC is notified by the ward nurse
A strategy discussion with the police
A disciplinary hearing is held by the trust
C.why: The LADO should be informed within one working day of all allegations against people who work with children.

whyNot.1: Regulator referral is advised on by the LADO; an HCA is not NMC-registered.
whyNot.2: A strategy discussion may follow, but the one-working-day duty is to the LADO.
whyNot.3: Disciplinary action follows the agreed process, not within one day.

C.q: A community children's nurse referred Ivy, 3, for neglect. Social care decided no further action. Ivy has since lost more weight and has untreated scabies. What is the most appropriate step?
options: Accept the decision, as social care has assessed
Ask the parents to self-refer to a charity
Wait until the next routine review in 3 months
Discuss with the safeguarding lead and escalate
C.why: Practitioners who disagree with a decision, especially with new concerns, should seek advice and use the local escalation procedure.

whyNot.0: Professional disagreement should be escalated, not accepted.
whyNot.1: Self-referral to a charity does not address continuing neglect.
whyNot.2: Waiting leaves Ivy at continuing risk.

C.q: Josh, 8, discloses that his father burned him with a cigarette. A strategy discussion is arranged. Who should, as a minimum, be involved?
options: A social worker, the GP and Josh's teacher
A social worker, health practitioners and police
The named nurse, police and Josh's parents
Health practitioners, the LADO and the head teacher
C.why: Working Together 2026: a local authority social worker, health practitioners and a police representative should, as a minimum, be involved.

whyNot.0: Police are part of the minimum; teachers may join.
whyNot.2: Parents do not take part in a strategy discussion.
whyNot.3: The LADO deals with allegations against staff; social care and police are needed.

reteach.title: The safeguarding clock
reteach.question: How do I remember all the Working Together timescales?

blocks.body: Day 1: social care decides what to do with your referral. If harm is suspected, a strategy discussion (social care, health, police). Within 15 working days of that: the initial conference. Within 10 working days of the conference: the core group. Within 3 months: the first review, then 6-monthly. Any assessment: 45 working days at most. Separate track: allegations against staff go to the LADO within 1 working day.

blocks.text: 15 runs from the strategy discussion, not the referral. 45 is a maximum, not a target.

explain.body: The local authority, ICB and chief officer of police share a joint and equal duty to make local safeguarding arrangements.

test.q: Which organisation represents health as a statutory safeguarding partner?
options: The local acute NHS trust
NHS England's regional team
The integrated care board
The GP practice
test.why: The ICB is the health safeguarding partner.

whyNot.0: NHS trusts are relevant agencies with s11 duties, not partners.
whyNot.1: NHS England is not one of the three local partners.
whyNot.3: GP practices are relevant agencies, not partners.

explain.body: Social care decides next steps within one working day. Any assessment is completed within 45 working days of referral.

test.q: A nurse made a referral two days ago and has heard nothing. What should she do?
options: Wait, as social care has 45 working days
Follow up and escalate if needed
Make a second referral to the police
Ask the family what has happened
test.why: A decision should be made within one working day; a referrer who hears nothing should follow up and escalate through local procedures.

whyNot.0: 45 working days is for assessments, not acknowledging a referral.
whyNot.2: A police referral is for immediate danger or crime, not a missed reply.
whyNot.3: Asking the family may put the child at risk.

explain.body: ICPC within 15 working days of the strategy discussion. Core group within 10 working days of the ICPC. First review within 3 months, then at most every 6 months.

test.q: When should the core group first meet after an initial child protection conference?
options: Within 5 working days
Within 15 working days
Within 1 calendar month
Within 10 working days
test.why: Working Together 2026: the core group meets within 10 working days of the initial conference.

whyNot.0: Five working days is not the timescale.
whyNot.1: 15 working days is the ICPC timescale.
whyNot.2: One month is not the Working Together timescale.

explain.body: Allegations against staff: senior manager immediately, LADO within one working day. Named doctor and nurse in each NHS provider; designated doctor and nurse at the ICB.

test.q: A parent alleges that a play specialist hurt her child. Who manages the oversight of this allegation across agencies?
options: The Local Authority Designated Officer
The ICB's designated doctor
The trust's freedom to speak up guardian
The Child Safeguarding Practice Review Panel
test.why: The LADO manages and oversees allegations against adults who work with children, paid or voluntary.

whyNot.1: Designated doctors give strategic health advice.
whyNot.2: The guardian supports staff raising concerns, not allegations against staff.
whyNot.3: The national panel reviews serious incidents.
